Caliber (artillery) - The length of the barrel (especially for larger guns) is often quoted in calibers. (wikipedia Article)

You see this a lot with naval artillery. It's one of those weird conventions that's been around for longer than anybody remembers. It was phased in with rifled artillery as the "pound" rating was phased out along with smoothbore naval guns.

Actually it has not been phased out. The caliber of if an artillery piece is the length of the barrel divided by the diameter of the projectile. The current M109 A6 self propelled 155 mm Howitzer is 39 caliber cannon. So you multiply 155 by 39 to get the length of the barrel of the cannon.
The part I was saying was phased out was the "pound" system. So the M109 can be called a 39 caliber cannon but you'll never see it called a twelve-pounder.
